chunks: And from him, from his father, raising it to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him),
he said: 'The women were mentioned in the presence of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), so he said: Do not consult them in the secret counsels, nor obey them among the near relatives'.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about consulting women in secret matters and kinship?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) delineates specific domains where male authority is emphasized, distinguishing between private deliberation (al-najwa) and familial obligations (dhī qarābah). Shia scholars often interpret this not as absolute dismissal of women's counsel, but as a guidance on maintaining household hierarchy and decisiveness in key areas, while acknowledging the broader Islamic principle of mutual consultation (shura) in general affairs.
